statement: editorial/profiles/artifact/visual-body-infographic.json sets composition.supporting_modules_max to 4 and its split_rule triggers when 'more than 4 major modules compete for attention'. This job's real topology (produced by an actual scripts/lib/chart-renderer.mjs renderDiagram() run, archived at evals/dogfood/2026-09-05-sue570-pilot/source-a/02-visual/report-diagram.mmd) has 8 nodes and 7 edges — the honest raw shape of the source article's argument (a 4-step mechanism chain plus a 3-step authority-shift chain plus one convergence node). The rendered SVG collapses this into 4 bordered top-level boxes, each containing 2-4 short internal labels, to satisfy supporting_modules_max literally. Nothing in visual-body-infographic.json's composition, split_rule, or acceptance sections defines whether 'module' means a top-level bordered region (this job's reading) or a leaf semantic unit (which would put this job at 8, well over the cap and past its own split_rule trigger). This job's own qa.density_recheck is honestly recorded as 'fail' and status 'qa_fail' rather than resolving the ambiguity unilaterally in the job's favor.

routing.modality_layer: VISUAL composition — visual/body-infographic supporting_modules_max ambiguity (top-level module vs. leaf node)
routing.rationale: editorial/feedback-routing.json's composition layer owns whether 'the composition does not clarify the semantic spec it was given, independent of brand tokens or rendering mechanics' — this is exactly that kind of layout/arrangement question, not a renderer defect (the renderer was run correctly and honestly disclosed as a hybrid hand-authoring step) and not a brand_profile issue (palette and materiality were followed correctly). Confidence is medium: this may already have an intended reading the profile author holds but did not write down, rather than a genuine unresolved gap — a single job re-interpreting an ambiguous term is not yet evidence the term needs to change, only evidence it should be written down explicitly one way or the other.
